BiblicalUsage: The Reed Sea is named once in the opening of Deuteronomy, as the place where Moses speaks to Israel in the wilderness. The name marks the sea Israel crossed, and the place where the journey began. It is the boundary between Egypt and the wilderness.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Reed Sea matters because it is the water God parted, and every retelling of the story starts from it.
RelatedEvents: The Exodus and the Red Sea
